intro: Lesson 86: Revision: living organisms, cells and enzymes; command words. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Which is a feature of ALL viruses?
questions.a: C) A protein coat. Viruses are particles with a protein coat around genetic material; they are not cells.

questions.q: Name the eight characteristics of living organisms (MRS GREN style).
questions.a: Nutrition, respiration, excretion, response, movement, control of internal conditions, reproduction, growth.

questions.q: Name a prokaryote on the specification.
Big question: what does an examiner want when a question says 'explain'?
questions.a: Reasons using correct science (how or why), linked with 'because' or 'so'.

questions.q: State two features of bacterial cells.
questions.a: Any two: no nucleus; circular chromosomal DNA; plasmids; cell wall; cell membrane; cytoplasm; ribosomes.
questions.model: 'State' means short facts, one mark each. Fact 1: no nucleus. Fact 2: plasmids present. No explanation needed.

questions.q: Explain why pepsin works in the stomach but amylase does not.
questions.a: The stomach is acidic (about pH 2) (1); pepsin's optimum is acidic, while amylase's active site is denatured at low pH (1).

questions.q: Give two differences between plant and fungal cells.
questions.a: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, not cellulose (1); fungi have no chloroplasts (1).

questions.q: Compare the structure of a palisade cell, a yeast cell and a bacterial cell. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Marks for: all have membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes (1); palisade and yeast have nuclei and mitochondria (1); palisade has chloroplasts, cellulose wall, large vacuole (1); yeast has a wall (chitin) and no chloroplasts (1); bacterium has no nucleus, circular DNA (1) and plasmids, no mitochondria (1).
questions.model: Teacher plans it first as a three-column table, then turns each row into a comparison sentence: 'All three have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and ribosomes, but only the bacterium lacks a nucleus...'

questions.q: Starch and amylase at 37 °C: the iodine colour stays blue-black for 20 minutes when the solution is boiled first. Explain.
questions.a: Boiling denatured the amylase (1); active site changed shape (1); starch not digested so iodine stays blue-black (1).

questions.q: Explain why viruses are not classed as living organisms.
questions.a: They show none of the characteristics on their own (1); they can only reproduce inside host cells (1).
